title: Cline Overview
claims: One agent core is presented behind Desktop, CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, SDK and Kanban.
Cline documents human-in-the-loop approval, per-card worktrees and dependency chains for Kanban.
notes: Public documentation; no installation or runtime test.

title: Cursor Agent
claims: Cursor documents tools, model and instructions as agent components.
Checkpoints are local file snapshots separate from Git.
notes: Closed implementation; mechanics are documentation claims only.

title: Cursor Run Modes
claims: Local modes distinguish allowlisted, sandboxed/classifier-reviewed and unrestricted calls.
Sandbox configuration controls workspace, network and path access.
notes: No security behavior was tested.

title: Cursor Background Agents
claims: Background agents run in isolated Ubuntu machines and push a separate branch.
Environment setup supports install/start commands, terminals and Dockerfile configuration.
notes: Product naming may now use Cloud Agents.

title: Zed Agent Panel
claims: Zed supports parallel threads, Git worktree isolation, checkpoints and change review.
Zed exposes tools, profiles, permissions and MCP in its Agent Panel.
notes: Native Zed behavior, not a claim about every ACP agent.

title: Zed External Agents
claims: ACP external agents run through their own process/provider relationship.
Zed hosts threads while external agents usually own runtime, auth, model, tools and native configuration.
notes: Primary source for the editor/agent ownership boundary.

tool: Using agent mode in your IDE
title: Using agent mode in your IDE
claims: Copilot agent mode chooses files, offers edits and commands, and iterates.
Terminal commands require approval by default and agent mode can use MCP.
notes: Applies to supported IDEs; availability can be administrator-controlled.

title: Custom agents
claims: Profiles are Markdown with YAML frontmatter and can restrict tools/MCP.
Subagents are separate-context delegated work and profile semantics can vary by environment.
notes: Closed service; profile portability caveat is documented.

title: OpenHands Sandboxes
claims: OpenHands V1 documents Docker, process and remote sandbox providers.
Docker is recommended while process execution is marked unsafe.
notes: Terminology changed from legacy runtime to sandbox.

title: OpenHands Runtime Architecture
claims: The documented Docker architecture separates agent/backend from container action execution.
Actions and observations communicate through a REST API.
notes: Public source documentation.

title: OpenHands README
claims: Agent Canvas can use local, Docker, VM, cloud and ACP-compatible agent backends.
Direct local agent-server execution has full filesystem access according to the README.
notes: Public source repository.

title: mini-SWE-agent control flow
claims: The default loop queries a model, executes actions and records observations until exit.
Documented interruption states include submit, limits, format, timeout and user interruption.
notes: Public source documentation.

title: mini-SWE-agent interactive mode
claims: Interactive CLI supports confirmation, yolo and human takeover modes.
Confirm is documented as the default mode.
notes: Public source documentation.

title: SWE-agent README
claims: SWE-agent states that mini-SWE-agent supersedes it.
SWE-agent describes one-YAML configuration and research orientation.
notes: Public source repository.

title: Devin Blueprint reference
claims: Blueprints separate initialize, maintenance and non-executed knowledge sections.
Snapshots save results while credentials are scrubbed from the saved image.
notes: Closed implementation; official documentation only.

title: Replit Agent task board
claims: Tasks progress through Drafts, Active, Ready and Done.
Accepted tasks run in isolated project copies until their work is applied.
notes: Closed implementation; official documentation only.

title: Replit Agent modes
claims: Modes expose speed/cost/capability tradeoffs.
Advanced options include automatic browser app testing and code optimization.
notes: Product capability claims were not tested.

title: Roo Code Docs
claims: The page states that the Roo Code extension was shut down on 2026-05-15.
The page identifies ZooCode as a community fork and describes historical modes, auto-approve, MCP and orchestrator concepts.
notes: Treat as archived/discontinued product documentation.

title: Zoo Code
claims: Zoo calls itself a community-maintained continuation of Roo Code.
It claims Roo-compatible settings, Apache-2.0 provenance, modes, diffs, MCP and semantic/partial-file context.
notes: Repository, license and release verification remain follow-up work.

title: Kilo Documentation
claims: Kilo documents VS Code, JetBrains and CLI surfaces.
Docs enumerate modes, custom rules, MCP, sessions, teams, automation and a model gateway.
notes: Permission and isolation details were not established in this pass.

title: What is Continue?
claims: Continue describes itself as an open source VS Code and JetBrains assistant.
Docs enumerate Agent, Chat, Edit, Autocomplete, CLI, YAML config, rules and MCP.
notes: Isolation semantics not established by this source.

title: Welcome to Lovable
claims: Lovable describes natural-language full-stack app generation backed by editable code.
Projects can sync with GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
notes: Closed hosted product.

title: AI assistance within Firebase Studio
claims: Coding workspace Gemini can update files, run terminal commands and interpret output.
App Prototyping workspace targets no-code Next.js/Firebase App Hosting/Genkit flows.
notes: Closed hosted product; separate workspace types are documented.

title: Bolt GitHub integration
claims: Bolt documents two-way GitHub synchronization, import, branch switching and automatic pull of GitHub changes.
It states that agent or manual edits passing runtime checks can auto-push to GitHub.
notes: Closed product; no agent-internal or isolation claim inferred.

title: Antigravity IDE overview
claims: Antigravity IDE documents asynchronous local agents and parallel work across workspaces.
Agents use editor, terminal and browser tools and create artifacts such as plans, diffs and browser recordings.
notes: Closed Google product; sandbox and approval detail still requires primary-source verification.

title: Google Antigravity Docs
claims: Google documents desktop command-center, CLI, SDK and IDE surfaces.
The platform includes workspaces, worktrees, skills, MCP and lifecycle hooks.
notes: Official documentation.

title: Junie by JetBrains
claims: Junie autonomously plans and executes multi-step work, including project edits, tests, terminal commands and external tools.
Junie can receive active-file and selected-text IDE context automatically.
notes: Closed product; permissions and isolation not established by this source.
